title: Add relation-aware SRD condition mechanics semantics
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

The current mechanics condition projection appears to collect condition mentions without distinguishing what the source text says about the condition. This is useful as a search hint, but unsafe as deterministic game-state logic.

Examples from the vk23 audit review:
- spell:shield can surface invisible because the prose says "An invisible barrier..." but the spell does not apply the Invisible condition.
- spell:sleep can surface charmed and unconscious, but charmed appears in an immunity clause while unconscious is the effect.
- spell:color-spray can surface blinded and unconscious, but unconscious appears in an exclusion/targeting clause.
- creature:death-dog has condition names in a trait that grants advantage against conditions, not conditions it applies.
- action:dodge mentions incapacitated because the benefit is lost if incapacitated; Dodge does not apply that condition.

This makes mechanics.conditions too ambiguous for deterministic tools. Runtime code must not treat raw condition mentions as "apply these conditions."

Acceptance criteria:
- Replace or augment raw condition mention projection with relation-aware semantics.
- Represent at least these relation classes, either as explicit fields or tagged entries:
  - applies / imposes condition
  - removes / ends condition
  - immunity or unaffected-by condition
  - advantage or disadvantage involving saves/checks against a condition
  - targeting exclusion or prerequisite involving a condition
  - descriptive mention only
- Add regression tests for Shield, Sleep, Color Spray, Death Dog Two-Headed, and Dodge.
- Update generated pack output and audit expectations so deterministic tools can identify condition application effects without false positives.
- Document the intended consumer contract: condition mentions are not authoritative state mutations unless relation says they are.
close_reason: parseConditions now classifies relation (applies/removes/immune/advantage/disadvantage/exclusion/mention) per sentence; regenerated pack; regression tests for all 5 named examples
